Subject: RFI follow-up: SCIM provisioning and delegated admin workflow

Jonas — thanks for the demo yesterday. We have a few follow-ups from our identity team around provisioning and admin controls before we move to procurement. Can you confirm the following at a high level?

1) Does Redwood support SCIM 2.0 for bulk provisioning and real-time updates (PATCH, PUT) for user attribute sync?
2) How are group-to-role mappings handled? Can we map SAML groups/SCIM groups to RBAC roles in a tenant-scoped way?
3) We need delegated admin scopes (read-only admin, user manager, billing admin). Can Redwood create custom admin roles and restrict them to specific org units?
4) Auditability: where are provisioning audit logs stored, and what retention policies are available? Can logs be exported to our SIEM (Splunk)?

We also need evidence: a short provisioning architecture diagram and an admin-role matrix for our auditors. If you have a SOC2 report we can share with procurement, that would help speed approvals.

Thanks,
Alan

Constellation Financial

Alan — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes (SCIM 2.0), yes (group->role mappings tenant-scoped), yes (custom admin roles and OU scoping), and yes (audit logs exportable to SIEM).

I put together a brief response below and attached the SCIM provisioning guide and admin-role matrix for your audit team. If your identity team prefers, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call to walk the diagrams and sample SCIM payloads.

Detailed responses:
1) SCIM 2.0: Redwood implements SCIM 2.0 with support for bulk operations and PATCH/PUT for incremental updates. We support incremental change tokens and offer configurable polling intervals for IdP-initiated syncs. Our SCIM endpoint enforces schema validation and supports custom extension attributes.

2) Group-to-role mapping: We provide a mapping layer where SCIM groups or SAML group assertions can be translated to Redwood RBAC roles. Mappings are managed per-tenant; you can scope mappings to an OU or a team. We also support conditional mappings based on attributes (e.g., department == "payments").

3) Delegated admin: Redwood supports first-class custom admin roles. You can create roles (e.g., user_manager, read_only_admin, billing_admin) and constrain them by tenant, OU, or tag. Role assignment supports both individual user and group binding. Temporary elevated access (time-boxed) is available via the console and API.

4) Auditability: Provisioning events are logged at the request level (create/update/delete), including actor, source IP, user agent, and before/after attribute snapshots. Logs are retained 90 days by default; longer retention is available as an add-on. We provide a Splunk HEC endpoint and S3 exports for archival. All exports include NDJSON with event types and timestamps.

I've attached: redwood-scim-provisioning-guide.pdf (architecture + sample payloads) and admin-role-matrix.csv (template). Also attaching a redacted SOC2 Type II summary; procurement can request the full report under an NDA.

Next steps: if that covers it, Marissa will coordinate procurement and our security SME (Kim) can join the technical call.

Best,

Elena — quick confirmation from the product/security side:

- Temporary elevation: elevations require re-authentication with MFA. The elevation event is recorded with actor, timestamp, justification, and duration. Session metadata (start/end times, IP, device fingerprint) is preserved. We do not capture full session recordings by default; that can be enabled for privileged sessions as part of an enterprise add-on.
- Near-real-time exports: webhooks (signed) are available for provisioning events; for high-volume customers we can set up a Kafka or Kinesis sink. Events include change vectors so partial payloads are compact.

I also populated admin-role-matrix.csv with Constellation-specific examples and uploaded a diagram to the Drive folder Marissa shared. Please see attachments. Happy to join the technical call on Wednesday.
